transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Jamie Ortiz (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Redwood Solutions), Tom Hsu (CISO, Silverlode), Lina Martinez (Head of Infra), Ravi Patel (Legal), Nora Green (ML Eng)

Summary (auto): quick intake to understand residency constraints for a cross-border quant analytics assistant. customer wants minimal surface for regulators and evidence bundles.

00:00 Jamie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll go through a handful of questions around where your data lives, logs, and what controls you need from a hosting perspective
00:14 Tom: thanks, Jamie, yeah quick context - we're a mid-market asset manager, most critical things are audit trails and strict geo residency for trade data, plus short retention for debug logs, we'd like to avoid broad egress where possible
00:30 Jamie: understood. I put Priya on the line to dive into the infra bits - Priya are you ok to take us through hosting options and where we typically see customers land?
00:41 Priya: sure, um hi all - so Redwood supports three main deployment patterns: hosted API (fast), dedicated pools (reserved GPUs), and private deployment (VPC or on-prem). For residency we commonly do either region-locked hosted or Private (VPC) depending on audit needs
01:05 Lina: can you explain 'region-locked hosted' - is that still Redwood managing keys or can we BYOK?
01:12 Priya: region-locked hosted means the control plane runs in our control region but compute and logs remain in the selected cloud region. For keys we offer BYOK via customer-managed KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private; hosted with BYOK is limited today but we can do a managed KMS flow with contractual guarantees
01:36 Tom: we need keys to never leave EU. If the control plane touches anything outside EU that's a concern for our regulator. also legal hold - we need immutable export when requested
01:50 Priya: right, for Private deployment you can do a control plane in your VPC and we support HSM/KMS so keys are fully customer managed, and audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. For hosted, we have contractual region-locks and data processing addendum, but the control plane can be US based unless you pick our private control plane option
02:20 Ravi: quick legal question - how granular are the logs? the ops team wants query-level logs but our compliance says we can't persist full prompts with PII beyond 30 days
02:33 Priya: two parts - Redwood has raw request logs for troubleshooting, but you can configure token-level redaction and a retention policy per tenant. We also have on-the-fly log masking where PII patterns can be redacted before being written. there may be slight perf impact for heavy masking
02:55 Nora: what's the perf hit? for our inference we need sub-200ms p99 on a lot of calls for prompt scoring
03:02 Priya: masking happens pre-storage, not on the generation path; primary latency impact is negligible on p99 if you use the dedicated pools. if you're on shared hosted, there could be minor variance. Also continuous batching and KV cache behavior can change tail latency a bit
03:26 Ethan: one nuance - if you enable prefix caching across customers we avoid duplication, but for residency you'd probably disable cross-tenant caching which affects unit cost
03:40 Lina: that matters, yes. cost is a factor but auditability and evidence packages are higher priority
03:47 Jamie: Tom, could you lay out the exact regulatory asks? e.g., retention windows, country list, and any SSO/socialized policy needs?
03:57 Tom: regulator requires that trade exec data not leave EU, retention for debug logs 30 days, audit-trail events 7 years, and any legal hold must be retrievable in native form within 72 hours. also a list of countries where host is permitted - currently just EU-27 and UK for those datasets
04:20 Priya: ok that's fairly precise. For audit-trail 7 years we typically write to cold object storage in-customer bucket (Private) or to region-locked storage with encryption and proper retention lifecycle. legal hold export we can do a bundled export with provenance metadata, signable manifests
04:44 Ravi: proof - can you provide evidence for tamper-proof logs? chain-of-custody stuff?
04:50 Priya: yes, we can provide append-only logs with checksums and S3 object lock or WORM on customer buckets for Private. For Hosted we provide signed evidence bundles and time-stamped manifests, but for regulator comfort customers in finance often prefer Dedicated or Private with S3 object lock under their control
05:10 Nora: any constraints on model weights staying in-region? our research team is paranoid about models trained on EU data staying in EU for inference
05:20 Priya: model binaries and weights can be pinned to region in Private and Dedicated. For hosted we maintain model catalog and can pin variants to regions; if it's a concern we recommend Private where everything is under your VPC and storage controls
05:37 Tom: ok curious about BYOK with HSM - does Redwood host a proxy or do we bring the HSM to our VPC?
05:44 Priya: two options: bring-your-own-key via KMS integration where you control keys in your cloud KMS/HSM; or we support HSM-backed key wrapping in Private where the HSM is customer-managed. Redwood doesn't hold plaintext keys in those flows
06:04 Lina: network: we need VPC peering or private connectivity, no public internet egress for some tenants
06:10 Priya: Private supports VPC peering or VPN. Dedicated can be placed in your cloud account with private networking. Hosted requires managed egress controls and IP allowlists; for strict no-egress you would want Private/on-prem
06:28 Ethan: small caveat - if you want full offline air-gapped inference (no control plane touch), that's our on-prem package and takes longer to deploy and higher operational cost
06:40 Tom: timeline: we're targeting a pilot in 3-4 weeks to validate redaction and the EU hosting flow, moving to production in Q3 - is that realistic?
06:49 Jamie: yes that's doable. typical pilot is 2-4 weeks for infra + 2 weeks for quality checks. we'll need your sample logs and a defined prompt set
07:01 Nora: we'll provide a 2-week prompt set, but we need to make sure we can do log-redaction rules iteratively. can you show us UI for redaction rules?
07:10 Priya: yes, Redwood Console has a redaction rules UI and you can add regex or custom PII detectors, and we keep a changelog for rule changes. we'll include screenshots in the packet
07:24 Ravi: any standard contractual language for jurisdictional lock and audit rights? we want to start with a paper NDA + DPA and then a limited pilot addendum
07:34 Jamie: we'll send a starter DPA and SLA and a pilot addendum; legal team can discuss any special jurisdictional language in the follow-up call
07:41 Tom: ok good. on logs retention - is there support for tiered retention? like 30 days in fast store, then 7 years in cold store but with redaction removed earlier?
07:52 Priya: yes tiered retention is supported. you can configure short-term raw logs for debugging (30d), and long-term audit artifacts with redaction/hashed pointers for 7 years. we also support legal-hold exemptions per artifact
08:10 Lina: are there any constraints around model rollback or can you guarantee model provenance snapshots? we need to link predictions to model version for audits
08:19 Priya: we keep model provenance and versioning in the catalog; predictions can be tied to model snapshot IDs and we can store immutables for audit. that's part of the evidence bundle
08:32 Tom: what about multi-geo failover? if EU region goes down, do we failover to US? that's a regulatory no-no for these data sets
08:39 Priya: routing policies support geo-fencing by dataset; you can pin a dataset to EU and set strict policy: no fallback outside EU. for higher availability we suggest multi-zone in-EU replication or Dedicated pools across AZs
08:55 Ethan: and you can configure automatic fallback to a lower-fidelity model in-region if capacity is constrained, instead of crossing geos
09:05 Ravi: audit request: we'll want a runbook for how Redwood will package evidence when regulators ask for data, including timelines and format
09:12 Jamie: agreed, we'll include a sample evidence runbook in the packet and show an example export of legal-hold + signed manifest
09:22 Nora: are there any red flags for HIPAA? we don't primarily process PHI but vendor checklist includes it
09:27 Priya: HIPAA controls overlap with SOC 2 and encryption; we support encryption at rest/in transit, role-based access, audit logs. if you need full HIPAA BAAs we'll have to scope separate but it's common enough that we can support it for HIPAA-bound workloads
09:44 Tom: competitors - we've talked to Anthropic about region locking and they had this concept of per-tenant compute islands, similar to Redwood Dedicated, curious on cost delta
09:53 Jamie: cost varies - Dedicated and Private cost more up-front but reduce unit cost for high volume and give stronger evidence for regulators. we'll include a cost model in the follow-up packet
10:05 Lina: last technical micro-question - can you redact embeddings and vector store snapshots? we want to minimize long-term retention of sensitive vectors
10:15 Priya: yes, vector snapshots can be redacted or hashed, and you can configure purge policies. embedding creation can also use in-region-only compute and KMS so vectors never leave region unencrypted
10:32 Tom: ok that's promising. next steps?
10:36 Jamie: recap: we'll send security packet (SOC2, ISO, DPA template), architecture diagram for Private/BYOK, redaction UI screenshots, pilot addendum and a preliminary cost estimate. Priya will validate BYOK/HSM and network playbook. Customer to send logs and prompt set. legal follow-up to firm up DPA language.
10:58 Tom: sounds good. thanks everyone.
11:02 Jamie: thanks all, we'll get those items out.
11:06 (call ends)
